THE ESSENTIALS

What is an SMC?

A Single Member Company (SMC) is a class of private limited company designed specifically for solo entrepreneurs. Under the Companies Act 2017, an SMC enjoys all the benefits of a corporate entity—including separate legal status and limited liability—while allowing one person to hold all shares and act as the sole director.

This is the ultimate structure for successful freelancers, solo tech founders, and independent consultants who want to scale their operations, hire a formal workforce, and open corporate bank accounts without giving away equity.

SMC Advantages

  • **No Partners Needed:** Retain 100% control of your business.
  • **Asset Shielding:** Your personal savings and property are protected from corporate lawsuits.
  • **Corporate Image:** Look established and trustworthy to international clients and B2B vendors.
THE RISK

Operating as a Solo Individual

If you are generating substantial revenue but remain unincorporated, you face several major bottlenecks.

Unlimited Liability

As a sole proprietor, you and your business are one entity. If your business fails or faces a lawsuit from a client, you are personally responsible for the debts.

Lost Enterprise Clients

Large corporations, government agencies, and international enterprises often require a registered corporate entity (SMC/Pvt Ltd) to sign vendor contracts.

Payment Processing Issues

Payment gateways like Stripe, PayPal (via proxies), or local banks scrutinize large transactions entering non-corporate accounts, frequently freezing funds.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

An SMC is a type of Private Limited Company where a single individual acts as both the sole director and the sole shareholder. It offers limited liability protection and corporate credibility while allowing a solo entrepreneur to retain full control.

An SMC is a legally distinct corporate entity recognized by the SECP. It protects your personal assets from business liabilities (limited liability), gives you a highly professional corporate image for B2B clients, and makes it easier to secure foreign remittances in corporate bank accounts.

Yes. If you decide to take on partners or investors in the future, your SMC can be legally converted into a standard Private Limited Company by transferring shares and appointing new directors with SECP.

We need a clear scan of your CNIC/Passport, your registered mobile number and email, 3 proposed company names, and the registered office address of the company.

No, that is the main benefit of an SMC. You do not need a partner. You hold 100% of the shares and act as the sole director.

SECP requires SMCs to nominate an individual (like a spouse, sibling, or parent) who will take over the shares and act as a temporary director in the event of the sole member's death. This ensures business continuity.

The entire process, from name reservation to the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, typically takes 7 to 10 working days.

Our professional fee for SMC registration is Rs. 30,000. This fee covers legal drafting, SECP filings, and NTN setup, but excludes the official government challan fees.

There is no massive capital requirement. You can register an SMC with an authorized capital of Rs. 100,000. This minimizes your government registration fees.

Absolutely. With your SECP Incorporation Certificate and corporate NTN, you can open a corporate bank account at any commercial bank in Pakistan.

Yes. SMCs are required to file an annual return (Form A/29) with SECP and an annual corporate tax return with the FBR.

Yes, it is highly recommended. Solo founders of software houses use SMCs to open corporate bank accounts, receive foreign IT remittances safely, and apply for PSEB registration to claim tax exemptions.
